en: Theravāda Vinayapiṭaka Cūḷavagga 20.
Bhikkhunikkhandhaka (The Chapter on the Nuns)
1. The Story of Mahāpajāpatī Gotamī.
At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling among the Sakyans at Kapilavatthu in the Nigrodha Monastery.
Then Mahāpajāpatī Gotamī approached the Blessed One; having approached and paid homage to the Blessed One, she stood to one side.
Standing to one side, Mahāpajāpatī Gotamī said this to the Blessed One:
“It would be well, Bhante, if women might receive the going-forth from the home life into homelessness in the Dhamma and Vinaya proclaimed by the Tathāgata.
“Enough, Gotamī; let it not please you that women receive the going-forth from the home life into homelessness in the Dhamma and Vinaya proclaimed by the Tathāgata.”
A second time...
and a third time, Mahāpajāpatī Gotamī said this to the Blessed One:
"It would be good, Bhante, if women might receive the going-forth from the home life into homelessness in the Dhamma and Vinaya proclaimed by the Tathāgata."
“Enough, Gotamī; let it not please you that women go forth from the home life into homelessness in the Dhamma and Vinaya proclaimed by the Tathāgata.

Then Mahāpajāpatī Gotamī, thinking, “The Blessed One does not permit women to go forth from the home life into homelessness in the Dhamma and Vinaya proclaimed by the Tathāgata,” [was deeply grieved].
Suffering, dejected, with tears on her face and weeping, she paid homage to the Blessed One, circumambulated him to the right, and departed.
Then the Blessed One, having stayed at Kapilavatthu for as long as he desired, set out on a wandering tour toward Vesālī.
Traveling by stages on his journey, he eventually arrived at Vesālī.
There the Blessed One was dwelling at Vesālī in the Great Wood, in the Gabled Hall.
Then Mahāpajāpatī Gotamī, having had her hair cut off and having donned saffron-colored robes, set out for Vesālī together with many Sakyan women.
Traveling by stages, she arrived at Vesālī, at the Great Wood, at the Gabled Hall.
Then Mahāpajāpatī Gotamī, with swollen feet and limbs covered in dust, distressed, dejected, tearful, and weeping, stood outside the gatehouse.
The Venerable Ānanda saw Mahāpajāpatī Gotamī standing outside the gatehouse with swollen feet and limbs covered in dust, distressed, dejected, tearful, and weeping.
Having seen her, he said this to Mahāpajāpatī Gotamī:
“Gotamī, why are you standing outside the gatehouse with swollen feet, your limbs covered in dust, suffering, dejected, tearful, and weeping?
“Because, venerable Ānanda, the Blessed One does not permit women to go forth from the home life into homelessness within the Dhamma and Vinaya proclaimed by the Tathāgata.

“In that case, Gotamī, stay right here for a moment while I ask the Blessed One for permission for women to go forth from the home life into homelessness within the Dhamma and Vinaya proclaimed by the Tathāgata.”
Then the Venerable Ānanda approached the Blessed One; having approached and paid homage to the Blessed One, he sat down to one side.
Sitting to one side, the Venerable Ānanda said this to the Blessed One:
"Venerable sir, this Mahāpajāpatī Gotamī is standing outside the gateway with swollen feet, her limbs covered in dust, suffering, dejected, tearful, and weeping."
“The Blessed One does not permit the going forth from the home life into homelessness for women within the Dhamma and Vinaya proclaimed by the Tathāgata.
“It would be well, Bhante, if women might receive the going forth from the home life into homelessness within the Dhamma and Vinaya proclaimed by the Tathāgata.
“Enough, Ānanda; do not find it pleasing that women should receive the going forth from the home life into homelessness within the Dhamma and Vinaya proclaimed by the Tathāgata.”
A second time...
and a third time, the Venerable Ānanda said this to the Blessed One:
"It would be good, Bhante, if women were to obtain the going-forth from the home life into homelessness in the Dhamma and Vinaya proclaimed by the Tathāgata."
“Enough, Ānanda, let it not please you that women go forth from the home life into homelessness in the Dhamma and Vinaya proclaimed by the Tathāgata.
Then the Venerable Ānanda thought:
“The Blessed One does not permit women to go forth from the home life into homelessness in the Dhamma and Vinaya proclaimed by the Tathāgata.”
"What if I were to request the Blessed One by another means for the going forth from the home life into homelessness for women within the Dhamma and Vinaya proclaimed by the Tathāgata?
Then the Venerable Ānanda said this to the Blessed One:
"Is it possible, Bhante, for women, within the Dhamma and Vinaya proclaimed by the Tathāgata, to go forth from the home life into homelessness?"
“Having gone forth, is it possible for a woman to realize the fruit of stream-entry, or the fruit of once-returning, or the fruit of non-returning, or the fruit of arhatship?

“Ānanda, it is possible for a woman, having gone forth from the home life into homelessness in the Dhamma and Vinaya proclaimed by the Tathāgata, to realize the fruit of stream-entry, the fruit of once-returning, the fruit of non-returning, and the fruit of arhatship.”

“Venerable sir, if women are capable—having gone forth from the home life into homelessness in the Dhamma and Discipline proclaimed by the Tathāgata—from realizing the fruit of stream-entry, the fruit of once-returning, the fruit of non-returning, or even the fruit of arahantship;

then, venerable sir, Mahāpajāpatī Gotamī has been of great service to the Blessed One: she is his maternal aunt, his nurse, his foster-mother, the giver of milk, who suckled him when his own mother had passed away.”
“It would be well, Bhante, if women were permitted to go forth from the home life into homelessness in the Dhamma and Vinaya proclaimed by the Tathāgata.
“If, Ānanda, Mahāpajāpatī Gotamī accepts eight weighty rules, that will suffice for her [ordination].”
Let there be full ordination.

A bhikkhunī who has been fully ordained for a hundred years must perform acts of salutation, rising from her seat, joining her palms in reverential salutation, and proper homage toward a bhikkhu who has been fully ordained on that very day.
This rule is to be honored, respected, revered, and venerated, and is not to be transgressed as long as life lasts.
A bhikkhunī must not observe the rains residence in a dwelling where no bhikkhus are present.
This rule also is to be honored, revered, esteemed, and worshipped throughout one’s life, and it is not to be transgressed.
Every half-month, a bhikkhunī should expect two things from the Saṅgha of bhikkhus:
The inquiry regarding the Uposatha, and the approaching for instruction.
This rule also is to be honored, revered, esteemed, and venerated, and is not to be transgressed as long as life lasts.
Having completed the rains residence, a bhikkhunī must perform the invitation ceremony before both Saṅghas with respect to three matters.
Whether by what is seen, or by what is heard, or by suspicion—
this rule also must be honored, revered, esteemed, and worshipped, and it is not to be transgressed for as long as life lasts.
A bhikkhunī who has committed a *garudhamma* must undergo the *mānatta* penance for a fortnight before both Saṅghas.
This rule also, having been honored, revered, esteemed, and worshiped, is not to be transgressed for as long as life lasts.
A probationary nun who has trained in the six rules for two years must seek full ordination from both Saṅghas.
This rule also, having been honored, revered, esteemed, and worshiped, is not to be transgressed for as long as life lasts.
A bhikkhunī must not, in any manner whatsoever, revile or abuse a bhikkhu.
This rule also is to be honored, respected, revered, and venerated for as long as life lasts; it is not to be transgressed.
From this day forward, the path of speech for bhikkhunīs toward bhikkhus is closed, while the path of speech for bhikkhus toward bhikkhunīs remains open.
"This rule too, having been honored, revered, esteemed, and worshiped, is not to be transgressed for as long as life lasts.
Ānanda, if Mahāpajāpatī Gotamī accepts these eight weighty rules, let that be her full admission.
Then the Venerable Ānanda, having learned the eight weighty rules in the presence of the Blessed One, approached Mahāpajāpatī Gotamī; having approached, he said this to Mahāpajāpatī Gotamī:
“Gotamī, if you would accept these eight weighty rules (garudhamma), that itself shall be your full ordination (upasampadā).
A bhikkhunī ordained for a hundred years must perform acts of salutation, rising from her seat, joining her palms, and respectful service toward a bhikkhu ordained on that very day.
This rule also is to be honored, revered, esteemed, and worshiped, and it is not to be transgressed as long as life lasts.”
A bhikkhunī must not spend the rains residence in a dwelling where no bhikkhus are present.
This rule, too, is to be honored, revered, esteemed, and worshiped; it is not to be transgressed for as long as life lasts.
Every half-month, a bhikkhunī should expect two things from the community of bhikkhus:
The inquiry regarding the Uposatha, and the approaching for instruction.
This rule also must be honored, revered, esteemed, and venerated, and it is not to be transgressed as long as life lasts.
Having completed the rains residence, a bhikkhunī must perform the invitation ceremony before both Saṅghas with respect to three matters.
Whether by what has been seen, or heard, or suspected.
This rule also, having honored, revered, esteemed, and worshipped it, is not to be transgressed for as long as life lasts.
A bhikkhunī who has committed a *garudhamma* must undergo the *mānatta* penance for a fortnight before both Saṅghas.
This rule also, having been honored, revered, respected, and worshipped, is not to be transgressed for as long as life lasts.
A probationary nun (sikkhamānā) who has trained in the training regarding the six rules for two years must seek full ordination (upasampadā) from both Saṅghas.
This rule also, having been honored, revered, respected, and worshipped, is not to be transgressed for as long as life lasts.
A bhikkhunī must not, by any means whatsoever, revile or abuse a bhikkhu.
This rule also is to be honored, revered, esteemed, and venerated for as long as life lasts, and it is not to be transgressed.
From this day forward, the path of speech for bhikkhunīs toward bhikkhus is closed, while the path of speech for bhikkhus toward bhikkhunīs remains open.
“This rule, too, must be honored, revered, esteemed, and worshipped for as long as life lasts; it is not to be transgressed.
Gotamī, if you would accept these eight *garudhammas*, that itself shall be your full ordination.
“Venerable Ānanda, it is just as if a woman or a man—young, youthful, fond of ornaments, and having washed their head—”
"Just as one who, having received a garland of blue lotuses, a garland of jasmine, or a garland of atimuttaka flowers,
would receive them with both hands and place them upon the head—
the highest limb— even so, venerable Ānanda, do I accept these eight weighty rules for as long as life lasts, not to be transgressed."
Then the Venerable Ānanda approached the Blessed One; having approached and paid homage to the Blessed One, he sat down to one side.
Sitting to one side, the Venerable Ānanda said this to the Blessed One:
“Venerable sir, the eight weighty rules have been accepted by Mahāpajāpatī Gotamī; the Blessed One’s maternal aunt has received full ordination.”

“Ānanda, if women had not obtained the going-forth from the home life into homelessness in the Dhamma and Vinaya proclaimed by the Tathāgata, the holy life, Ānanda, would have lasted long; the True Dhamma would have remained for a thousand years.
But since, Ānanda, women have now gone forth from the home life into homelessness in the Dhamma and Vinaya proclaimed by the Tathāgata, the holy life will not last long now, Ānanda.
The True Dhamma will now remain for only five hundred years.”
"Just as, Ānanda, whatever families have many women and few men are easily plundered by thieves and bandits;
even so, Ānanda, in whatever Dhamma and Discipline women obtain the going-forth from the home life into homelessness, that holy life does not endure for long.
Just as, Ānanda, when a disease called white rust falls upon a thriving field of rice, that rice field does not endure for long."
In the same way, Ānanda, in whatever Dhamma and Vinaya women obtain the going-forth from the household life into homelessness, that holy life does not endure for long.
Just as, Ānanda, when a disease called *mañjiṭṭhikā* falls upon a flourishing sugarcane field, that sugarcane field does not endure for long;
even so, Ānanda, in whatever Dhamma and Vinaya women obtain the going-forth from the household life into homelessness, that holy life does not endure for long.
“Just as, Ānanda, a man might build a dam around a great reservoir beforehand, precisely so that the water does not overflow, even so, Ānanda,
have I prescribed these eight weighty rules for the bhikkhunīs, which must not be transgressed for as long as life lasts.
The eight weighty rules for the bhikkhunīs are concluded.
3. The Granting of Full Ordination for Bhikkhunīs.
Then Mahāpajāpatī Gotamī approached the Blessed One; having approached and paid homage to the Blessed One, she stood to one side.
Standing to one side, Mahāpajāpatī Gotamī said this to the Blessed One:
“Venerable sir, how should I conduct myself toward these Sakyan women?
Then the Blessed One instructed, urged, inspired, and gladdened Mahāpajāpatī Gotamī with a discourse on the Dhamma.

Having been instructed, urged, inspired, and gladdened by the Blessed One’s discourse on the Dhamma, Mahāpajāpatī Gotamī paid homage to the Blessed One, circumambulated him keeping her right side toward him, and departed.
Then the Blessed One, having given a discourse on the Dhamma on this occasion and in this context, addressed the bhikkhus:
“I allow, bhikkhus, that bhikkhus confer full ordination upon bhikkhunīs.
Then those bhikkhunīs said this to Mahāpajāpatī Gotamī:
“The noble ladies are not ordained, whereas we are ordained;
for it has been thus prescribed by the Blessed One that nuns are to be ordained by monks.
Then Mahāpajāpatī Gotamī approached the Venerable Ānanda, and having approached and paid homage to the Venerable Ānanda, she stood to one side.
Standing to one side, Mahāpajāpatī Gotamī said this to the Venerable Ānanda:
“Venerable Ānanda, these bhikkhunīs have said this to me:
‘The noble lady was not fully ordained; we are the ones who are fully ordained.’”
"For it has been thus prescribed by the Blessed One that bhikkhus should confer full ordination upon bhikkhunīs.
Then the Venerable Ānanda approached the Blessed One; having approached and paid homage to the Blessed One, he sat down to one side.
Sitting to one side, the Venerable Ānanda said this to the Blessed One:
“Venerable sir, Mahāpajāpatī Gotamī says this:
‘Venerable Ānanda, these bhikkhunīs say to me:
“The noble lady has not been fully ordained; we have been fully ordained.”’”
“For it has been thus ordained by the Blessed One that bhikkhus should ordain bhikkhunīs.
“Ānanda, at the very moment the eight *garudhammas* were accepted by Mahāpajāpatī Gotamī, she was ordained.
Then Mahāpajāpatī Gotamī approached the Venerable Ānanda; having approached, she paid homage to the Venerable Ānanda and stood to one side.
Standing to one side, Mahāpajāpatī Gotamī said this to the Venerable Ānanda:
“Venerable Ānanda, I ask a favor of the Blessed One.
It would be well, venerable sir, if the Blessed One would allow monks and nuns to perform salutations, rising from their seats, joining their palms, and respectful duties according to seniority.”
Then the Venerable Ānanda approached the Blessed One; having approached and paid homage to the Blessed One, he sat down to one side.
Sitting to one side, the Venerable Ānanda said this to the Blessed One:
"Venerable sir, Mahāpajāpatī Gotamī says this:"
“Venerable Ānanda, I request one favor from the Blessed One.
It would be well, venerable sir, if the Blessed One would permit monks and nuns to perform salutation, rising from their seats, joining of palms, and proper respectful conduct according to seniority.

“Ānanda, it is impossible, it is out of the question, that the Tathāgata would permit women to perform salutation, rising from their seats, joining of palms, and proper respectful conduct [toward him].”
“Ānanda, these followers of other sects, whose teachings are poorly expounded, will not even perform salutations, rising from their seats, joining of palms, or respectful duties toward women;
how much less, then, would the Tathāgata authorize such salutations, rising from one’s seat, joining of palms, or respectful duties toward women?
Then the Blessed One, having given a discourse on the Dhamma on this occasion and in this context, addressed the bhikkhus:
“Monks, one should not perform prostrations, rising to greet, joining of palms, or respectful service toward women.
Whoever should do so commits an offense of wrong-doing.
Then Mahāpajāpatī Gotamī approached the Blessed One; having approached and paid homage to the Blessed One, she stood to one side.
Standing to one side, Mahāpajāpatī Gotamī said this to the Blessed One:
“Venerable sir, regarding those training rules for bhikkhunīs that are shared with the bhikkhus, how, venerable sir, should we proceed in regard to those training rules?
“Gotamī, regarding those training rules for bhikkhunīs that are shared with the bhikkhus, train in those training rules in the same way that the bhikkhus train.”
“But, Bhante, regarding those training rules for bhikkhunīs that are not shared with the bhikkhus, how should we proceed with those training rules?
“Gotamī, regarding those training rules for bhikkhunīs that are not shared with the bhikkhus, train yourselves in those training rules exactly as they have been laid down.
Then Mahāpajāpatī Gotamī approached the Blessed One; having approached, she paid homage to the Blessed One and stood to one side.
Standing to one side, Mahāpajāpatī Gotamī said this to the Blessed One:
“It would be well, Bhante, if the Blessed One would teach me the Dhamma in brief, so that having heard the Dhamma from the Blessed One, I might dwell alone, withdrawn, diligent, ardent, and resolute.
“Those qualities, Gotamī, which you should know—”
These states lead to passion, not to dispassion; they lead to bondage, not to liberation;
they lead to accumulation, not to diminution; they lead to great desire, not to fewness of wishes;
they lead to lack of contentment, not to contentment; they lead to social entanglement, not to seclusion; they lead to laziness.
They do not lead to the arousal of energy, but to being difficult to support, not to being easy to support.
You should categorically understand, Gotamī:
"This is not the Dhamma, this is not the Vinaya, this is not the Teacher’s instruction."
But as for those qualities, Gotamī, that you might know:
"These qualities lead to dispassion, not to passion; they lead to detachment, not to bondage;
they lead to diminution, not to accumulation; they lead to fewness of desires, not to great desire; they lead to contentment..."
They lead to contentment, not discontent; they lead to seclusion, not to socializing; they lead to the arousal of energy, not to laziness;
they lead to being easy to support, not to being difficult to support.
You should hold this, Gotamī, as an absolute certainty.
“This is the Dhamma, this is the Vinaya, this is the Teacher’s instruction.
Now at that time, the Pātimokkha was not being recited for the bhikkhunīs.
They reported this matter to the Blessed One... [as before]...
“I allow you, monks, to recite the Pātimokkha for the nuns.
Then it occurred to the monks:
“By whom, then, should the Pātimokkha be recited for the nuns?”
They reported this matter to the Blessed One.
“I allow you, monks, for monks to recite the Pātimokkha for the bhikkhunīs.
Now at that time, monks would go to the bhikkhunīs’ dwelling place and recite the Pātimokkha for the bhikkhunīs.
People complained, grumbled, and spread it about, saying, "These are their wives;
these are their mistresses; now they will take their pleasure with them.
They reported this matter to the Blessed One.
“Monks, the Pātimokkha should not be recited for the bhikkhunīs by bhikkhus.
Whoever should recite it, there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
Monks, I allow the bhikkhunīs to recite the Pātimokkha for the bhikkhunīs.”
The bhikkhunīs did not know,
“The Pātimokkha should be recited in this way.
They reported this matter to the Blessed One.
“I allow you, monks, to instruct the bhikkhunīs:
‘You should recite the Pātimokkha in this way.
Now at that time, the bhikkhunīs did not make amends for their offenses.
They reported this matter to the Blessed One:
“Monks, an offense must not be left unexpiated by a bhikkhunī.
Whoever does not expiate it commits an offense of wrong-doing.”
The bhikkhunīs did not know how an offense was to be confessed.
They reported this matter to the Blessed One.
“I allow you, monks, to instruct the bhikkhunīs:
‘In this way you should make amends for an offense.
Then it occurred to the monks:
“By whom, then, should the offense of the bhikkhunīs be received?
They reported this matter to the Blessed One.
“I allow, monks, that the offense of the bhikkhunīs be received by the bhikkhus.”
Now at that time, when the bhikkhunīs saw a bhikkhu on a carriage road, in a cul-de-sac, or at a crossroads,
they would set their bowls on the ground, arrange their upper robes over one shoulder, sit down on their heels,
and with palms joined, confess their offenses.
People criticized, complained, and grumbled, saying, “These are their wives;
these are their mistresses. Having treated them with contempt at night, they are now asking for forgiveness.
They reported this matter to the Blessed One.
“Monks, an offense of nuns must not be accepted by monks.
Whoever should accept one, there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
Monks, I allow that an offense of nuns be accepted by nuns.”
The bhikkhunīs did not know how an offense was to be accepted;
they reported this matter to the Blessed One.
“I allow you, monks, to instruct the nuns:
‘You should accept an offense in this way.
Now at that time, no formal legal act was being performed for the nuns.
They reported this matter to the Blessed One.
“I allow you, monks, to perform formal acts for the nuns.
Then it occurred to the monks:
“By whom, then, should the formal act for the bhikkhunīs be performed?
They reported this matter to the Blessed One.
“I allow you, monks, to have the formal act for the bhikkhunīs performed by monks.”
Now at that time, nuns who had performed the formal act (of censure) would see a monk on a carriage road,
in a cul-de-sac, or at a crossroads; they would set down their bowls on the ground, arrange their upper robes over one shoulder,
sit down on their heels, and with palms joined, ask for forgiveness, thinking, "Surely this is how it ought to be done."
People likewise complained, grumbled, and spread it about, saying:
“These are their wives; these are their mistresses. Having treated them with contempt at night, they are now asking for forgiveness.
They reported this matter to the Blessed One.
“Monks, a formal act (kamma) for bhikkhunīs must not be performed by bhikkhus.
Whoever should do so commits an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
Monks, I allow a formal act for bhikkhunīs to be performed by bhikkhunīs.”
The bhikkhunīs did not know,
"This is how the formal act should be performed.
They reported this matter to the Blessed One.
“I allow you, monks, to instruct the nuns, saying:
‘You should perform the formal act in this way.
Now at that time, the nuns were living in the midst of the Saṅgha having fallen into quarreling, strife, and dispute, piercing one another with the weapons of their tongues.
They were unable to settle that legal dispute.
They reported this matter to the Blessed One:
“I allow you, monks, for monks to settle a legal dispute among the nuns.”
Now at that time, the monks were settling a legal dispute for the nuns.
While that legal dispute was being decided, some nuns were seen who were subject to formal acts and who had committed offenses.
The nuns spoke thus:

“It would be well, venerable sir, if the noble ones themselves were to perform the formal acts for the bhikkhunīs, and if the noble ones themselves were to receive the confession of the bhikkhunīs’ offenses;
for it has been so prescribed by the Blessed One that legal matters concerning bhikkhunīs should be settled by bhikkhus.
They reported this matter to the Blessed One.
“I allow, monks, that after the monks have brought a formal act against the nuns, they hand it over to the nuns so that the nuns may carry out the formal act against those nuns;
and that after the monks have brought a charge of an offense against the nuns, they hand it over to the nuns so that the nuns may receive the confession of the offense from those nuns.
Now at that time, a nun who was a pupil of the nun Uppalavaṇṇā had followed the Blessed One for seven years, mastering the Vinaya.
For that nun who was muddled in mindfulness, whatever she grasped was lost again and again.
Then that bhikkhunī heard:
"The Blessed One, it is said, intends to go to Sāvatthī."
Then it occurred to that bhikkhunī:
"For seven years I followed the Blessed One, mastering the Vinaya.
Yet, because I was forgetful, every time I grasped it, it was lost."
"It is indeed difficult for a woman to follow the Teacher for as long as life lasts. How, then, should I proceed?
Then that bhikkhunī reported this matter to the bhikkhunīs.
The bhikkhunīs reported this matter to the bhikkhus.
The bhikkhus reported this matter to the Blessed One:
"I allow you, bhikkhus, to have the bhikkhunīs instructed in the Vinaya."
The first recitation section is finished.
Then the Blessed One, having stayed at Vesālī for as long as he pleased, set out on a wandering tour toward Sāvatthī.
Traveling by stages on his tour, he eventually arrived at Sāvatthī.
At that time, the Blessed One was staying at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove,
Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery. Now on that occasion, the group of six monks drenched the bhikkhunīs with muddy water,
thinking, “Perhaps they will fall in love with us.”
They reported this matter to the Blessed One.
"Monks, a monk must not splash nuns with muddy water.
Whoever should splash them, there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa)."
“I allow you, monks, to carry out a disciplinary act against that monk.
Then it occurred to the monks,
“What kind of disciplinary act should be carried out?”
They reported this matter to the Blessed One.
“Monks, that monk should be made unworthy of salutation by the Saṅgha of bhikkhunīs.
Now at that time, the group of six monks, having uncovered their bodies, showed them to the bhikkhunīs... [and so on].
They exposed their thighs to show them to the bhikkhunīs; they exposed their private parts to show them to the bhikkhunīs; they flirted with the bhikkhunīs;
they engaged in socializing with the bhikkhunīs, thinking, "Perhaps they might fall in love with us.
They reported this matter to the Blessed One.
“Monks, a monk must not expose his body to the nuns; he must not expose his thighs to the nuns;
he must not expose his private parts to the nuns; he must not flirt with the nuns;
he must not engage in socializing with the nuns.”
Whoever should engage in such association incurs an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
“I allow you, monks, to carry out disciplinary action against that monk.
Then it occurred to the monks:
“What disciplinary action, then, should be performed?
They reported this matter to the Blessed One.
“Monks, that monk should be made unworthy of salutation by the Saṅgha of bhikkhunīs.”
Now at that time, the group-of-six bhikkhunīs sprinkled a bhikkhu with muddy water,
thinking, "Perhaps he will feel passion for us.
They reported this matter to the Blessed One.
“Monks, a monk must not be splashed with muddy water by a bhikkhunī.
Whoever should so splash him commits an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
Monks, I allow that disciplinary action (daṇḍakamma) be carried out against that bhikkhunī.”
Then it occurred to the monks,
"What disciplinary action (daṇḍakamma) should be performed?
They reported this matter to the Blessed One.
“Monks, I allow you to place an obstruction,” he said.
When an obstruction was placed, they would not take it up.
They reported this matter to the Blessed One.
“Monks, I allow you to suspend the exhortation.
Now at that time, the group-of-six bhikkhunīs would expose their bodies and show them to the bhikkhus;
they would expose their breasts and show them to the bhikkhus; they would expose their thighs and show them to the bhikkhus; [and they would expose] their private parts...
Having opened them, they showed them to the bhikkhus; they illuminated them for the bhikkhus;
they engaged with the bhikkhus, thinking, "Perhaps they might feel affection for us.
They reported this matter to the Blessed One.
“Monks, a bhikkhunī must not expose her body to show it to the bhikkhus...

she must not expose her breasts to show them to the bhikkhus, she must not expose her thighs to show them to the bhikkhus, she must not expose her private parts to show them to the bhikkhus; she must not address the bhikkhus, nor [be addressed] by the bhikkhus...”
She should be associated with [the task].
Whoever should associate her, there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
“I allow you, monks, to carry out disciplinary action against that bhikkhunī.”
Then it occurred to the monks,
"What disciplinary action (daṇḍakamma) should be performed?
They reported this matter to the Blessed One.
“Monks, I allow you to place an obstruction,” [the Blessed One said].
When an obstruction was placed, they would not take it up.
They reported this matter to the Blessed One.
“I allow you, monks, to suspend the exhortation.
Then it occurred to the monks:
“Is it allowable to perform the Uposatha together with a nun for whom the exhortation has been suspended, or is it not allowable?”
They reported this matter to the Blessed One.
“Monks, the Uposatha should not be performed together with a nun who has been suspended from the exhortation, as long as that legal issue has not been settled.
Now at that time, the Venerable Udāyī, having suspended the exhortation, set out on a wandering tour.
The bhikkhunīs complained, grumbled, and spread it about, saying:
"How can the venerable Udāyī set aside the exhortation and depart on tour?
They reported this matter to the Blessed One.
“Monks, you should not set out on a journey after having suspended the exhortation.
Whoever should so depart commits an offense of wrong-doing.
Now at that time, fools and the incompetent were suspending the exhortation.
They reported this matter to the Blessed One:
“Monks, an instruction should not be suspended by one who is ignorant and incompetent.
Whoever should suspend it incurs an offense of wrong-doing.”
Now at that time, the monks suspended the exhortation without basis and without cause.
They reported this matter to the Blessed One:
"Monks, the exhortation must not be suspended without basis and without cause."
“Whoever should set it aside, there is an offense of wrong-doing.
Now at that time, the monks, having set aside the exhortation, did not provide a formal decision.
They reported this matter to the Blessed One.
“Monks, the formal decision must not be made without setting aside the exhortation.
Whoever should fail to do so commits an offense of wrong-doing.
At that time, however, the bhikkhunīs did not go for the exhortation.
They reported this matter to the Blessed One.
“Monks, a bhikkhunī must go for the exhortation.
Whoever does not go shall be dealt with according to the rule.”
Now at that time, the entire community of bhikkhunīs went for the exhortation.
People complained, grumbled, and spread it about, saying:
"These are their wives; these are their mistresses; now they will take pleasure with them."
They reported this matter to the Blessed One:
“Monks, the entire Saṅgha of bhikkhunīs should not go for the exhortation.
If they were to go, there would be an offense of wrong-doing.”
“I allow you, monks, for four or five bhikkhunīs to go for the exhortation.
At that time, however, four or five bhikkhunīs went for the exhortation.
People, as before, complained, grumbled, and became indignant:
"These are their wives; these are their mistresses; now they will take delight with them.
They reported this matter to the Blessed One.
"Monks, one should not go for the exhortation with four or five bhikkhunīs."
If they should go, there is an offense of wrong-doing.
I allow you, monks, two or three nuns to go for the exhortation.

Having approached a single monk, having arranged her upper robe over one shoulder, having bowed at his feet, having sat down on her heels, and having extended her hands in reverential salutation, she should speak to him thus:
“Venerable sir, the community of bhikkhunīs pays homage at the feet of the community of bhikkhus and requests the opportunity to approach for the exhortation.
May the community of bhikkhunīs, venerable sir, receive the opportunity to approach for the exhortation.
Then that bhikkhu, having approached the reciter of the Pātimokkha, should speak to him thus:
‘Venerable sir, the community of bhikkhunīs pays homage at the feet of the community of bhikkhus and requests the approach for the exhortation;
may the community of bhikkhunīs, venerable sir, receive the approach for the exhortation.
The reciter of the Pātimokkha should say:
‘Is there any monk appointed as an instructor of the nuns?
If there is a monk appointed as an instructor of the nuns, the reciter of the Pātimokkha should say:
‘The monk named so-and-so has been appointed as the instructor of the nuns; let the community of nuns approach him.’
If there is no monk who has been appointed as an instructor of the nuns, the reciter of the Pātimokkha should say:
“Which venerable one is able to instruct the nuns?
If someone is able to instruct the nuns and is endowed with eight qualities, he should be appointed and told:
“‘The monk named so-and-so has been appointed as the instructor of the bhikkhunīs; let the community of bhikkhunīs approach him.
If no one is able to instruct the bhikkhunīs, the reciter of the Pātimokkha should say:
‘There is no monk who has been appointed as the instructor of the bhikkhunīs; let the community of bhikkhunīs attain spiritual excellence through inspiring conduct.’”
Now at that time, the monks did not accept the exhortation.
They reported this matter to the Blessed One:
"Monks, the exhortation must not be neglected."
“Whoever should accept it, there is an offense of wrong-doing.
Now at that time, a certain bhikkhu was foolish.
Some bhikkhunīs approached him and said this:
“Venerable sir, please accept my exhortation.
“Sister, I am a fool;
how could I accept an exhortation?”
“Take up the exhortation,
venerable sir; for it has been so ordained by the Blessed One that bhikkhus must give exhortation to the bhikkhunīs.”
They reported this matter to the Blessed One.
“Monks, I allow you to receive the exhortation from all except for a fool.
Now at that time, a certain monk was ill.
The bhikkhunīs approached her and said,
“Venerable lady, please accept our instruction.
She replied, “Sisters, I am ill.”
“How shall I receive the exhortation?
“Receive the exhortation, venerable sir;
for it has been so prescribed by the Blessed One:”
“Excepting the fool, the exhortation should be received by the rest.
They reported this matter to the Blessed One.
“Monks, I allow you to receive the exhortation from the rest, excepting the fool and excepting the sick.”
Now at that time, a certain monk was about to depart for a village.
The bhikkhunīs approached him and said,
"Venerable sir, please accept our invitation for instruction."
“I am going away, sister;
how can I receive the exhortation?
“Receive the exhortation, venerable sir.”
"For it has been thus prescribed by the Blessed One:
'Excepting the fool and excepting the sick, the rest must receive the exhortation.
They reported this matter to the Blessed One.
“Monks, I allow you to receive the exhortation from all except for one who is ignorant, one who is ill, and one who is about to travel.
Now at that time, a certain monk was dwelling in the forest.
Some bhikkhunīs approached him and said this:
“Venerable sir, please accept my exhortation.
“Sister, I dwell in the forest;
how can I accept an exhortation?”
“Take the exhortation, venerable sir;
for it has been so prescribed by the Blessed One:
‘Excepting one who is a fool, excepting one who is ill, and excepting one who is about to travel, the exhortation must be taken by the rest.’”
They reported this matter to the Blessed One.
“Monks, I allow a forest-dwelling monk to receive the exhortation and to make an appointment, saying:
‘I will return here.’”
Now at that time, the monks, having received the exhortation, did not announce it.
They reported this matter to the Blessed One:
"Monks, the exhortation must not be left unannounced."
“Whoever does not report it commits an offense of wrong-doing.
Now at that time, the monks, having received the exhortation, did not return [to report].
They reported this matter to the Blessed One.
“Monks, the exhortation must not be declined.
Whoever should decline it commits an offense of wrong-doing.
Now at that time, the nuns did not go to the appointed place.
They reported this matter to the Blessed One.
“Monks, a bhikkhunī must not fail to go to the rendezvous.
Whoever does not go commits an offense of wrong-doing.”
Now at that time, the bhikkhunīs were wearing long waistbands and were bending their ribs with them.
People criticized, grumbled, and complained about it, saying:
“…just like householders who indulge in sensual pleasures.”
They reported this matter to the Blessed One:
“Monks, a long waistband must not be worn by a bhikkhunī.
Whoever should wear one, there is an offense of wrong-doing.”
“I allow, monks, a single-layered waistband for a bhikkhunī, but she must not bend the ribs with it.
Whoever should bend them, there is an offense of wrong-doing.
Now at that time, the bhikkhunīs were bending the ribs with a strip of cloth made from melted-down material... [etc.]
They bind the shoulder-straps with a leather strap;
they bind the shoulder-straps with a cloth strap;
they bind the shoulder-straps with a cloth braid.
They tie the ends together with a cloth-strip;
they tie the ends together with a band of cloth;
they tie the ends together with a cord of cloth.
They bend the ribs with a *coḷavaṭṭi* (a strip of cloth).
They bend the ribs with a *suttaveṇī* (a cord of thread).
They bend the ribs with a *suttavaṭṭī* (a coil of thread).
People criticized, complained, and spread it about, saying,
“…just like householders who enjoy sensual pleasures.
They reported this matter to the Blessed One.
“Monks, a nun must not bend the ribs with a strip of cloth made of melted material … nor must she bend the ribs with a coil of thread.
Whoever should do so commits an offense of wrong-doing.”
Now at that time, the bhikkhunīs were having their hips rubbed with a stone...

[as before] ...they were having their hips pounded with a cow’s jawbone; they were having their hands pounded, having their hand-gloves pounded, having their feet pounded, having their foot-gloves pounded, having their thighs pounded, having their faces pounded, and having their gums pounded.
People complained, grumbled, and became indignant... [as before] ...
“It is just like householders’ wives who enjoy sensual pleasures.
They reported this matter to the Blessed One.
“Monks, a bhikkhunī must not have her hips rubbed with a bone…” [and so forth].
“Teeth and gums must not be rubbed.
Whoever should have them rubbed commits an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
Now at that time, the group-of-six bhikkhunīs were smearing their faces... [and so on]...
They massage their faces, powder their faces, mark their faces with red arsenic, apply body ointments, apply face cosmetics, and apply both body and face cosmetics.
People criticized, complained, and spread it about, saying,
“...just like householders who enjoy sensual pleasures.”
They reported this matter to the Blessed One.
“Monks, a bhikkhunī must not smear her face...
she must not rub her face, nor grind powder for her face, nor paint her face with red arsenic, nor apply body ointment, nor apply facial ointment, nor apply both body and facial ointments.”
"Whoever should do so, there is an offense of wrong-doing. Now at that time, the group-of-six bhikkhunīs were applying collyrium to their eyes,
applying forehead marks, looking with a side-long glance, and standing within range of sight.
They cause dancing to be performed; they establish courtesans; they set up taverns; they set up slaughterhouses; they open shops;
they engage in lending for interest; they engage in trade; they keep male slaves; they keep female slaves; they keep laborers;
they keep female laborers; they keep animals; they live on a diet of *harītakī* fruits.
They were weaving and wearing felt cloaks.
People criticized, complained, and spread it about, saying,
“...just like householders who enjoy sensual pleasures.”
They reported this matter to the Blessed One:
“Monks, a nun must not apply collyrium to her eyes...
she must not apply decorative marks, she must not look about with a sidelong glance, she must not stand where there is light, and she must not watch a dance.”
It should be caused to be built; a prostitute should not be established, a tavern should not be set up, a slaughterhouse should not be established,
a shop should not be opened, usury should not be practiced, trade should not be engaged in, a male slave should not be maintained,
a female slave should not be maintained, a male laborer should not be maintained, and a female laborer should not be maintained.
"One should not have an animal attend [to one]; one should not distribute *harītakī* fruit; one should not carry a sandal-bag.
Whoever should carry one, there is an offense of wrong-doing (*dukkaṭa*).
Now at that time, the group-of-six bhikkhunīs wore robes that were entirely blue... [and so on].
They wear robes that are entirely yellow; they wear robes that are entirely red; they wear robes that are entirely madder-red;
they wear robes that are entirely black; they wear robes that are entirely dyed with mahāraṅga;
they wear robes that are entirely dyed with mahānāma; they wear robes with uncut fringes.
They wore robes with long borders, they wore robes with flowered borders, they wore robes with fruit-patterned borders, they wore bodices, and they wore *tirīṭaka* garments.
People complained, grumbled, and spread it about... [as before]...
“It is just like householders who enjoy sensual pleasures.
They reported this matter to the Blessed One.
“Monks, a bhikkhunī should not wear robes that are entirely blue... [and so on]...”
“Tirīṭaka cloth must not be worn.
Whoever should wear it, there is an offense of wrong-doing.
Now at that time, a certain bhikkhunī, while dying, spoke thus:
“After my passing, let my requisites belong to the Saṅgha.
Regarding this, the monks and nuns quarreled, saying, “They belong to us! They belong to us!”
They reported this matter to the Blessed One:
“Monks, if a nun, while passing away, should say, ‘After my death, let my requisites belong to the Saṅgha,’ the Bhikkhu Saṅgha has no ownership over them; they belong to the Bhikkhunī Saṅgha alone.”
“Monks, if a female trainee, or if a novice nun, should die and say:
‘After my passing, let my requisites belong to the Saṅgha,’ in that case the community of monks has no ownership over them; they belong to the community of nuns alone.”
“Monks, if a bhikkhu, while passing away, should say:
‘After my death, let my requisites belong to the Saṅgha,’ then in that case the community of bhikkhunīs has no ownership; these belong to the community of bhikkhus alone.
If it is a sāmaṇera, monks … [and so on].”
“Monks, if a male lay follower...
or if a female lay follower...
or if anyone else, monks, while passing away, should say thus:”
‘After my passing away, let my requisites belong to the Saṅgha’—in that case, the Bhikkhunī Saṅgha has no ownership over them; they belong only to the Bhikkhu Saṅgha.
Now at that time, a certain woman who had been a former wrestler went forth among the Bhikkhunīs.
Seeing a weak Bhikkhu on the street, she struck him with her shoulder-blade and knocked him down.
The bhikkhus complained, grumbled, and spread it about,
saying, "How can a bhikkhunī give a blow to a bhikkhu?
They reported this matter to the Blessed One.
“Monks, a nun must not strike a monk.
Whoever should do so commits an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
Monks, I allow a nun, upon seeing a monk, to step aside from afar and give way.”
Now at that time, a certain woman whose husband was away from home became pregnant by an adulterer.
Having caused an abortion, she said this to a bhikkhunī who was a frequent visitor to her family:
"Come, noble lady, take this fetus out in a bowl."
Then that bhikkhunī, having placed the fetus in her alms-bowl and covered it with her outer robe, departed.
Now at that time, a certain bhikkhu who was wandering for alms had made this vow:
"Whatever alms-food I first receive, I shall not consume it without first giving some to a bhikkhu or a bhikkhunī."
Then that bhikkhu, seeing that bhikkhunī, said this to her:
“Come now, sister, accept some almsfood.
“Enough, venerable sir,” she replied.
A second time...
and a third time, that bhikkhu said to that bhikkhunī:
"Come now, sister, accept some almsfood."
“Enough, noble lady. “Sister, I have made this commitment:
‘Whatever alms I first receive, I shall not consume it without having given some to a monk or a nun.’”
“Come now, sister, accept this almsfood.
Then that bhikkhunī, being pressured by that bhikkhu, brought it out and showed him the bowl:
“Look, venerable sir, at the embryo in the bowl!”
"And do not tell anyone.
Then that monk complained, grumbled, and became indignant, saying,
"How can a bhikkhunī take a fetus out with her alms-bowl?"
Then that bhikkhu reported this matter to the bhikkhus.
Those bhikkhus who were of few desires... [as before]... were indignant, disparaged it, and complained, saying:
"How can a bhikkhunī take a fetus out with her alms-bowl?"
They reported this matter to the Blessed One:
“Monks, a fetus must not be removed by a nun with a bowl.
Whoever should remove it incurs an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).”
“I allow you, monks, for a bhikkhunī who has seen a bhikkhu, to take it out and show him the bowl.
Now at that time, the group-of-six bhikkhunīs, having seen a bhikkhu, turned [the bowl] over and showed him the base of the bowl.
The bhikkhus complained, grumbled, and became indignant, saying:
“How indeed can the group-of-six bhikkhunīs, upon seeing a bhikkhu, turn [the bowl] around and show him the base of the bowl?
Then those bhikkhus reported this matter to the Blessed One.
“Bhikkhus, a bhikkhunī, upon seeing a bhikkhu, must not turn [the bowl] around and show him the base of the bowl.”
If she should show it [to him], there is an offense of wrong-doing.
I allow, monks, that when a nun has seen a monk, she may lift up her bowl and show it to him;
and whatever alms-food is in the bowl, with that he should be invited.”
Now at that time, a male organ had been discarded on a street in Sāvatthī.
The bhikkhunīs gazed at it intently.
People raised a clamor.
Those bhikkhunīs were embarrassed.
Then those bhikkhunīs went to their dwelling and reported this matter to the bhikkhunīs.
Those bhikkhunīs who were few in desires... [as before]... were indignant, complained, and grumbled:
“How indeed can the bhikkhunīs gaze intently at the male organ?
Then those bhikkhunīs reported this matter to the bhikkhus,
and the bhikkhus reported this matter to the Blessed One.
“Monks, a nun must not gaze at the male organ.
Whoever should so gaze commits an offense of wrong-doing.
Now at that time, people were giving material gifts to the monks.
The monks gave [the requisites] to the bhikkhunīs.
People complained, grumbled, and spread it about:
"How can these venerable ones give away to others what was given for their own use?"
“We ourselves do not know how to give a gift,” they said,
and they reported this matter to the Blessed One.
“Monks, what has been given for one’s own use should not be given to others.”
"Whoever should give [it], there is an offense of wrong-doing.
Now at that time, foodstuffs had become abundant for the monks.
They reported this matter to the Blessed One.
“I allow you, monks, to give it to the Saṅgha.
It became even more abundant.
They reported this matter to the Blessed One.
“I allow you, monks, to give even what belongs to an individual.
Now at that time, the stored-up food of the monks had become abundant.
They reported this matter to the Blessed One.
“I allow you, monks, having had the stored food received by the nuns, to consume it.
Now at that time, people gave food to the nuns,
and the nuns gave it to the monks.
People criticized, complained, and grumbled:
“How can these bhikkhunīs give away what was given for their own use?
We too do not know how to give a gift!”
They reported this matter to the Blessed One.
“Monks, what has been given to a nun for her own use must not be given to others.
Whoever should give it away commits an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).”
Now at that time, foodstuffs had become abundant for the bhikkhunīs.
They reported this matter to the Blessed One.
“I allow you, bhikkhus, to give it to the Saṅgha,” he said.
It became even more prevalent.
They reported this matter to the Blessed One:
“Monks, I allow you to give even what belongs to an individual.”
Now at that time, stored-up food had accumulated among the bhikkhunīs.
They reported this matter to the Blessed One.
“I allow you, monks, for the bhikkhunīs to consume stored-up food after having it received by bhikkhus.”
Now at that time, lodgings were abundant for the monks but not for the nuns.
The nuns sent a messenger to the presence of the monks, saying:
"It would be good, venerable sirs, if the masters would give us lodgings on a temporary basis."
They reported this matter to the Blessed One.
“I allow you, monks, to give lodgings to the bhikkhunīs for a limited time,” he said.
Now at that time, bhikkhunīs who were menstruating sat down and lay down upon upholstered couches and upholstered chairs.
The bedding was smeared with blood.
They reported this matter to the Blessed One:
“Monks, a bhikkhunī should not sit down or lie down upon a covered bed or a covered chair.”
Whoever should sit down or lie down [there], there is an offense of wrong-doing.
“I allow you, monks, a lodging-cloth,” he said.
The lodging-cloth became stained with blood.
They reported this matter to the Blessed One.
“Monks, I allow a cloth for the binding,” he said.
But the cloth fell off.
They reported this matter to the Blessed One.
“Monks, I allow you to tie it with a thread and fasten it to the thigh.
The thread broke.
They reported this matter to the Blessed One.
“I allow you, monks, a wrap garment and a waistband,” he said.
Now at that time, the group of six bhikkhunīs wore a waistband at all times.
People criticized, grumbled, and complained,
saying, “She is just like a housewife who indulges in sensual pleasures.
They reported this matter to the Blessed One.
“Monks, a belt must not be worn by a bhikkhunī at all times.
Whoever should wear one, there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
Monks, I allow a belt for one who is menstruating.”
The second recitation section is finished.
Now at that time, those who had received full ordination were seen to be:

those without sexual characteristics, those with only the marks of sex, those without blood, those with constant discharge of blood, those who constantly wear menstrual cloths, those with a continuous flow, those with a fistula, female eunuchs, those with masculine traits, those with a split urethra, and those with both sets of sexual organs.
They reported this matter to the Blessed One.
“I allow you, monks, to ask one who is receiving full ordination about the twenty-four obstructive conditions.
And thus, monks, should she be asked:”
‘Are you not without signs? Are you not merely a sign? Are you not bloodless? Are you not constantly menstruating? Are you not constantly wearing menstrual cloths? Are you not discharging [fluids]?
Are you not a sikharaṇī? Are you not a paṇḍaka woman? Are you not a man-like woman? Are you not one with a ruptured womb? Are you not a hermaphrodite?’
Do you have such diseases as leprosy, boils, ringworm, consumption, or epilepsy? Are you a human being?
Are you a woman? Are you free? Are you without debt? Are you not a royal servant?
“Have you been permitted by your mother and father, and by your husband?
Are you twenty years of age? Is your bowl and robe complete? What is your name? What is the name of your preceptor?
At that time, the monks were questioning the nuns regarding the obstructing conditions.
Those seeking full ordination were embarrassed and abashed, and they were unable to answer.
They reported this matter to the Blessed One.
“Monks, I allow that one who has been ordained on one side be fully ordained in the community of monks after she has been purified in the community of nuns.”
Now at that time, the nuns, not having been instructed, were questioning those seeking full ordination regarding the obstructing conditions.
Those seeking full ordination became embarrassed and abashed; they were unable to answer.
They reported this matter to the Blessed One.
“Monks, I allow you to instruct [the candidates] first and afterwards to ask them about the obstructing conditions.
Yet they instructed them right there in the midst of the Saṅgha.
The candidates for ordination became embarrassed and abashed in that very way; they were unable to answer.
They reported this matter to the Blessed One.
“I allow you, monks, after having instructed [a candidate] in private, to question him about the obstructing states in the midst of the Saṅgha.
And furthermore, monks, he should be instructed in this way.”
First, she should be made to take a preceptor.
Having had her take a preceptor, the bowl and robes should be explained to her:

"This is your bowl; this is the outer robe (saṅghāṭī); this is the upper robe (uttarāsaṅga); this is the inner robe (antaravāsaka); this is the bodice (saṅkaccika); this is the bathing-cloth (udakasāṭikā)."
“Go and stand in that place.
Thus do fools and the incompetent give instructions.
When those seeking ordination are poorly instructed, they become distressed and abashed; they are unable to respond.
They reported this matter to the Blessed One:
“Monks, a foolish and incompetent woman must not be instructed.
Whoever should instruct her incurs an offense of wrong-doing.”
“I allow, monks, a learned and competent bhikkhunī to give instruction.
They gave instruction without being appointed.
They reported this matter to the Blessed One.
“Monks, one who has not been formally appointed should not instruct.
Whoever should so instruct commits an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
I allow you, monks, to instruct one who has been formally appointed.”
And furthermore, monks, she should be appointed in this way:
either she should appoint herself, or another should appoint her.
And how should she appoint herself?
The Saṅgha should be informed by a competent and experienced nun:
“Let the noble Saṅgha hear me.
So-and-so desires the full ordination from the noble lady so-and-so.”
‘If it seems appropriate to the Saṅgha, may I, [name], instruct [name].
In this way one should appoint oneself.
And how should another be appointed by another?
The Saṅgha should be informed by a competent and experienced nun:
“Let the noble Saṅgha listen to me.
So-and-so desires the full ordination from the noble lady So-and-so.”
‘If it seems appropriate to the Saṅgha, let such-and-such a woman instruct such-and-such a woman.
In this way, one person should be appointed by another.
Having approached the person seeking full ordination, that appointed nun should speak to her as follows:
‘Listen, [Name].
This is the time for truth, the time for what is factual.
When asked in the midst of the Saṅgha regarding what has arisen, you should say “it exists” if it is so, and you should say “it does not exist” if it is not.’
Do not be distressed; do not be dejected.
They will question you thus:
"Are you without marks? Are you merely marked? Are you bloodless? Are you constantly bleeding? Do you always wear rags?"
Do you not have discharging nose, do you not have a runny nose, are you not a female eunuch, are you not a male eunuch, are you not one with a split organ, are you not a hermaphrodite?
Do you have such ailments as these?
Do you have leprosy, boils, eczema, consumption, or epilepsy?
Are you a human being? Are you a woman? Are you free? Are you not in debt? Are you not a royal servant?
Have you been permitted by your parents and your husband?
‘Are you twenty years of age? Is your bowl and robe complete? What is your name? What is the name of your preceptor?
They come together.
They should not come together.
Having arrived first, the instructor should inform the Saṅgha:
“Let the noble Saṅgha listen to me.
The lady named so-and-so desires the full ordination from the noble lady named so-and-so.”
"She has been instructed by me:
'If it is appropriate for the Saṅgha, let so-and-so come.
She should be told: 'Come.'"

Having had her arrange her upper robe over one shoulder, having had her pay homage at the feet of the nuns, having had her sit in the kneeling position, and having had her extend her joined palms in reverential salutation, she should be made to request full ordination as follows:
“Venerable ladies, I request full ordination from the Saṅgha.
Venerable ladies, may the Saṅgha lift me up out of compassion.”
For a second time, noble ladies, I request full ordination from the Saṅgha.
May the Saṅgha, out of compassion, lift me up.
For a third time, noble ladies, I request full ordination from the Saṅgha.
‘May the Saṅgha, noble ladies, lift me up out of compassion.
A competent and capable bhikkhunī should inform the Saṅgha:
‘Let the Saṅgha, noble ladies, hear me.
This woman, [name], desires the full ordination from the noble lady [name].
If it is agreeable to the Saṅgha, I shall question [name] regarding the obstructing conditions.
Listen, [name].
This is the time for your truth, the time for what is real.
I ask you about what has arisen: that which exists should be said to "exist," and that which does not exist should be said to "not exist.
You are not without signs... [and so forth].
“What is your name, and what is the name of your preceptor?
A competent and capable bhikkhunī should inform the Saṅgha:
“Venerable ladies, let the Saṅgha hear me. [She states her name and that of her preceptor.]”
This woman, [name], desires full ordination from the noble lady [name].
She is pure regarding the obstructing conditions, and her bowl and robes are complete.
[Name] requests full ordination from the Saṅgha, with the noble lady [name] as her preceptor.
If it seems appropriate to the Saṅgha, let the Saṅgha ordain so-and-so with Venerable so-and-so as her preceptor.
This is the motion.
Let the noble Saṅgha listen to me.
This woman, [name], desires the full ordination from the noble lady [name].
She is pure with respect to the obstructing factors, and her bowl and robes are complete.
[Name] requests full ordination from the Saṅgha, with the noble lady [name] as her preceptor.
The Saṅgha confers full ordination upon [name], with the noble lady [name] as preceptor.
Whichever noble lady approves of the full ordination of [name] with the noble lady [name] as preceptor, let her be silent;
whichever does not approve, let her speak.
A second time I speak this matter...
A third time I speak this matter:
Let the noble Saṅgha hear me.
This woman, [name], seeks full ordination from the noble lady [name].
She is pure with respect to the obstructing factors, and her bowl and robes are complete.
[Name] requests full ordination from the Saṅgha, with the noble lady [name] acting as her preceptor.
The Saṅgha confers full ordination upon [name], with the noble lady [name] as preceptor.
Whichever noble lady approves of the full ordination of [name] with the noble lady [name] as preceptor, let her be silent;
whichever does not approve, let her speak.
“[The candidate] has been fully ordained by the Saṅgha with such-and-such a lady as preceptor.
It is pleasing to the Saṅgha; therefore, it is silent. Thus do I understand this.

Immediately taking her [to the monks], she should approach the community of monks, cause her to arrange her upper robe over one shoulder, cause her to pay homage at the feet of the monks, cause her to sit in the kneeling position, and cause her to extend her joined palms in reverence, and then she should be made to request full ordination:
‘Venerable ladies, I, [name], am seeking full ordination from the venerable lady [name].
I have been ordained on one side in the community of bhikkhunīs and am pure.
Venerable ladies, I request full ordination from the Saṅgha.’
Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha uplift me out of compassion.
Venerable sirs, I, [name], am seeking full ordination from the venerable lady [name].
I have been ordained on one side in the Bhikkhunī Saṅgha and am pure.
A second time, noble ladies, I request full ordination from the Saṅgha.
May the Saṅgha, out of compassion, lift me up.
Noble ladies, I, [name], am seeking full ordination through the noble lady [name].
‘I am fully ordained in the Bhikkhunī Saṅgha; I am pure.
For a third time, noble ladies, I entreat the Saṅgha for full ordination.
May the Saṅgha, out of compassion, lift me up.’”
A competent monk who knows the procedure should inform the Saṅgha:
“Venerable sirs, let the Saṅgha hear me.
This woman, named so-and-so, desires the full ordination from the one named so-and-so.”
She has received the full admission (upasampadā) as one among the community of bhikkhunīs and is pure.
So-and-so requests full admission from the Saṅgha with So-and-so as her preceptor (pavattinī).
If it is agreeable to the Saṅgha, let the Saṅgha grant full admission to So-and-so, with So-and-so as her preceptor.
This is the motion.
Let the Sangha, venerable sirs, hear me.
This person named so-and-so desires the full ordination from the one named so-and-so.
She has been ordained as a nun in the Order of Bhikkhunīs and is pure.
So-and-so requests ordination from the Sangha with So-and-so as her preceptor.
The Sangha ordains So-and-so with So-and-so as her preceptor.
Whichever venerable one approves of the full ordination of [Name] with [Name] as the presiding teacher, let him be silent;
whichever does not approve, let him speak.
For the second time, I speak this matter... [repetition as above].
For a third time I speak on this matter:
Let the Saṅgha hear me, venerable sirs.
This person named so-and-so desires the full ordination from the person named so-and-so.
She has been ordained in the Bhikkhunī Saṅgha; she is pure.
So-and-so requests ordination from the Saṅgha with So-and-so as her preceptor.
The Saṅgha ordains So-and-so with So-and-so as her preceptor.
Whichever venerable one approves of the full ordination of [Name] by [Name] as the presiding nun, let him be silent;
whoever does not approve, let him speak.
[Name] has been fully ordained by the Saṅgha with [Name] as the presiding nun.
“The Saṅgha consents, therefore it is silent; thus do I hold it.

At that very moment, the shadow must be measured, the measure of the season must be announced, the portion of the day must be announced, and the recitation must be announced. The bhikkhunīs should be told:
“Explain to her the three supports and the eight things not to be done.”
Now at that time, the bhikkhunīs were wasting their time while waiting for seats in the dining hall.
They reported this matter to the Blessed One. [The Blessed One said:
"I allow, monks, eight bhikkhunīs to sit according to seniority, and the rest according to the order of their arrival."
Now at that time, the bhikkhunīs—
thinking, "The Blessed One has authorized eight bhikkhunīs to sit according to seniority, while the rest sit according to the order of their arrival"—
everywhere barred the eight bhikkhunīs from sitting according to seniority and allowed the rest to sit according to the order of their arrival.
They reported this matter to the Blessed One.
“I allow you, monks, in the dining hall, for eight bhikkhunīs, according to seniority, and for the rest, according to the order of arrival;
elsewhere, in all other places, they must not be obstructed from sitting according to seniority.”
"Whoever should prevent [the invitation], there is an offense of wrong-doing.
Now at that time, the bhikkhunīs did not perform the invitation ceremony (pavāraṇā).
They reported this matter to the Blessed One.
“Monks, a bhikkhunī must perform the invitation ceremony (*pavāraṇā*).
Whoever does not perform it is to be dealt with according to the rule.
Now at that time, the bhikkhunīs, having performed the invitation ceremony among themselves, did not perform the invitation ceremony for the Saṅgha of bhikkhus.
They reported this matter to the Blessed One.
“Monks, a bhikkhunī, having performed the invitation ceremony herself, must not fail to invite the Saṅgha of bhikkhus.
Whoever does not invite shall be dealt with according to the Dhamma.”
Now at that time, the bhikkhunīs were performing the invitation ceremony together with the bhikkhus in a single group and made a great clamor.
They reported this matter to the Blessed One.
"Bhikkhus, a bhikkhunī should not perform the invitation ceremony together with the bhikkhus in a single group."
"Whoever should invite [for the Pavāraṇā ceremony], there is an offense of wrong-doing.
Now at that time, the bhikkhunīs spent their time inviting while it was before the meal.
They reported this matter to the Blessed One.
“Monks, I allow you to perform the *pavāraṇā* ceremony after the meal.
They performed the *pavāraṇā* after the meal and it became the wrong time.
They reported this matter to the Blessed One.
“I allow you, monks, having performed the *pavāraṇā* ceremony for the community of nuns on this day, to perform the *pavāraṇā* ceremony for the community of monks on the following day.
Now at that time, the entire community of nuns, while performing the *pavāraṇā*, made a great clamor.
They reported this matter to the Blessed One.
“I allow you, monks, to appoint one bhikkhunī who is competent and capable to invite the Saṅgha of bhikkhus on behalf of the Saṅgha of bhikkhunīs.
And this, monks, is how she is to be appointed.
First, a bhikkhunī should be requested; having requested her, a competent and capable bhikkhunī should inform the Saṅgha:
“Let the noble Saṅgha hear me.
If it seems appropriate to the Saṅgha, let the Saṅgha appoint the bhikkhunī named so-and-so to invite the Bhikkhu Saṅgha on behalf of the Bhikkhunī Saṅgha.”
This is the motion.
Let the noble Saṅgha hear me:
the Saṅgha appoints the bhikkhunī named so-and-so for the sake of the Bhikkhunī Saṅgha, to perform the invitation ceremony (*pavāraṇā*) toward the Bhikkhu Saṅgha.
Whichever noble lady approves of the appointment of the bhikkhunī named so-and-so to invite the Saṅgha of bhikkhus on behalf of the Saṅgha of bhikkhunīs, let her be silent;
whichever does not approve, let her speak.
The Saṅgha has approved the bhikkhunī named so-and-so to invite the Saṅgha of bhikkhus on behalf of the Saṅgha of bhikkhunīs.
‘The Saṅgha consents, therefore it is silent; thus do I understand this.

Then that appointed nun, having taken the community of nuns with her, should approach the community of monks, arrange her upper robe over one shoulder, pay homage at the feet of the monks, sit down on her haunches, raise her joined palms, and speak to them thus:”
“Venerable sirs, the community of bhikkhunīs invites the community of bhikkhus regarding what has been seen, heard, or suspected.
May the venerable community of bhikkhus speak to the community of bhikkhunīs out of compassion; seeing [the fault], she will make amends.”
A second time, noble ladies...
a third time, noble ladies, the Saṅgha of bhikkhunīs invites the Saṅgha of bhikkhus regarding what has been seen, heard, or suspected.
“Speak, noble lady; let the Saṅgha of bhikkhus speak out of compassion for the Saṅgha of bhikkhunīs, so that seeing [the fault], they will make amends.

Now at that time, the bhikkhunīs were canceling the Uposatha of the bhikkhus, canceling the Pavāraṇā, issuing commands, initiating formal accusations, demanding an opportunity [to speak], reproaching, and bringing charges.
They reported this matter to the Blessed One.
“Monks, a nun must not cancel the Uposatha of a monk;
even if she cancels it, it is as if it were not cancelled.
For her who cancels it, there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).”
The invitation ceremony (pavāraṇā) must not be suspended;
even if suspended, it is as if not suspended.
For one who suspends it, there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
One must not make her speak; even if she has been made to speak, it is as if it were not done;
for one who does so, there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
A formal act of reconciliation (anuvāda) should not be instituted;
even if instituted, it is as if not instituted.
For one who institutes it, there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
An opportunity [to confess] must not be granted;
even if granted, it is as if not granted;
for her who grants it, there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
She should not be accused;
even if accused, she is as if unaccused.
For the one who accuses her, there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
"She is not to be reminded; even if she has been reminded, she is as if not reminded;
for the one who reminds her, there is an offense of wrong-doing."

Now at that time, monks were canceling the Uposatha of the nuns, canceling the Pavāraṇā, issuing commands, instigating accusations, demanding an opportunity for confrontation, accusing them, and making formal charges against them.
They reported this matter to the Blessed One.
“Monks, I allow a monk to cancel the Uposatha of a nun.”
Even if it has been set aside, it is well-set-aside;
there is no offense for one who sets it aside.
One may set aside the invitation ceremony (*pavāraṇā*).
Even if it has been set aside, it is well-set-aside;
there is no offense for one who sets it aside.
To make [the monk] subject to being spoken to;
Even if it has been well-prepared,
there is no offense for one who is making it.
To initiate a formal accusation;
Even if it has been set up, it is well-set up;
there is no offense for one who sets it up.
To request space;
Even if he causes [it] to be done, it is well-done;
there is no offense for one who causes it to be done.
To exhort;
Even when urged, she is well-urged;
there is no offense for one who urges her.
To remind her;
“Even if she has been sent for, she has been properly sent for;
there is no offense for the one who sends her.
Now at that time, the group-of-six bhikkhunīs traveled by means of a vehicle.
“Even with a man accompanied by a woman, or a woman accompanied by a man,
people were indignant, disparaged, and complained, saying:
‘...just as if at the confluence of the Ganges and the Mahī.’”
They reported this matter to the Blessed One.
“Monks, a bhikkhunī must not travel by vehicle.
Whoever should so travel is to be dealt with according to the rule.”
Now at that time, a certain bhikkhunī was ill and was unable to go on foot.
They reported this matter to the Blessed One.
"I allow, monks, a vehicle for one who is ill," [the Blessed One said].
Then it occurred to the bhikkhunīs,
"Is this yoked for women, or is it yoked for men?
They reported this matter to the Blessed One.
“I allow, monks, a handcart drawn by women or drawn by men.
Now at that time, a certain bhikkhunī became very unwell due to the jolting of a vehicle.
They reported this matter to the Blessed One.
“I allow, monks, a palanquin and a litter.
Now at that time, the courtesan Aḍḍhakāsī had gone forth among the bhikkhunīs;
she wished to go to Sāvatthī.
“I shall receive full ordination in the presence of the Blessed One.
Now some scoundrels heard that the courtesan Aḍḍhakāsī intended to go to Sāvatthī.
They blocked the road.
The courtesan Aḍḍhakāsī heard that "the scoundrels have indeed blocked the road."
She sent a messenger to the Blessed One, saying:
"I desire to receive full ordination;
how indeed should I proceed?"
Then the Blessed One, having given a discourse on the Dhamma on this occasion and in this context, addressed the bhikkhus:
“I allow you, bhikkhus, to confer full ordination even by means of a messenger. They conferred full ordination by means of a bhikkhu-messenger.
They reported this matter to the Blessed One:
"Monks, one should not grant full ordination with a monk as a messenger.
Whoever should so ordain, there is an offense of wrong-doing."
They confer full ordination using a trainee nun as a messenger...
they confer full ordination using a male novice as a messenger...
they confer full ordination using a female novice as a messenger... [and so forth].
“They ordain by messenger for one who is foolish and incompetent.
‘Monks, one should not ordain by messenger for one who is foolish and incompetent.
Whoever should ordain [her], there is an offense of wrong-doing.’”
"I allow, monks, a competent and capable nun to confer full ordination by means of a messenger.

That nun who acts as the messenger, having approached the Saṅgha, having arranged her upper robe over one shoulder, having bowed at the feet of the monks, having sat down on her heels, and having extended her hands in reverential salutation, should speak thus:
'Venerable sirs, the lady so-and-so desires full ordination through the lady so-and-so.'"
She has received full ordination in the community of bhikkhunīs and is pure.
Due to some obstacle, she does not come.
Venerable sirs, the one named so-and-so requests full ordination from the Saṅgha.
Venerable sirs, let the Saṅgha uplift her, out of compassion.
Venerable sirs, the lady named so-and-so desires full ordination from the lady named so-and-so.
She has been ordained on one side in the Bhikkhunī Saṅgha and is pure.
She has not come because of some obstacle.
For a second time, venerable sirs, so-and-so requests full ordination from the Saṅgha.
May the Saṅgha, out of compassion, lift her up.
Venerable sirs, the lady named so-and-so desires ordination from the lady named so-and-so.
She has been ordained on one side in the community of bhikkhunīs and is pure;
however, she does not come because of some obstacle.
"A third time also, venerable ladies, so-and-so requests ordination from the Saṅgha.
May the Saṅgha, out of compassion, lift her up.
A competent and capable monk should inform the Saṅgha:
‘Let the Saṅgha hear me, venerable sirs.
So-and-so desires ordination through so-and-so.
She has been ordained on one side in the Bhikkhunī Saṅgha and is pure.’
She has not come because of some obstacle.
So-and-so requests full ordination from the Saṅgha with so-and-so as her preceptor.
If it is agreeable to the Saṅgha, let the Saṅgha grant full ordination to so-and-so with so-and-so as her preceptor.
This is the motion.
Let the Saṅgha, venerable sirs, hear me.
So-and-so desires the full ordination from so-and-so.
She has received the full ordination in the community of bhikkhunīs and is pure.
Due to a certain obstacle, she does not come.
So-and-so requests full ordination from the Saṅgha with So-and-so as her preceptor.
The Saṅgha confers full ordination upon [name], with [name] as the preceptor.
Whichever venerable one approves of the full ordination of [name] with [name] as the preceptor, let him be silent;
whoever does not approve, let him speak.
A second time I speak this matter...
A third time I speak this matter.
Let the Saṅgha, venerable sirs, hear me.
So-and-so is seeking full ordination from So-and-so.
She has been ordained on one side in the community of bhikkhunīs and is pure.
She does not come because of some obstacle.
So-and-so requests full ordination from the Sangha with So-and-so as her preceptor.
The Sangha grants full ordination to So-and-so with So-and-so as her preceptor.
Whichever venerable one approves of the full ordination of So-and-so with So-and-so as her preceptor, let him be silent.
"Whoever does not agree with this should speak.
This person named so-and-so has been authorized by the Saṅgha with such-and-such as her instructor.
It is pleasing to the Saṅgha; therefore, by silence, we hold it to be so."
“Right now the shadow must be measured; the measure of the season must be announced; the portion of the day must be announced; the recitation must be announced; and the bhikkhunīs should be told:
‘Explain to her the three supports and the eight things not to be done.
Now at that time, the bhikkhunīs were dwelling in the forest.
Rogues corrupted them.
They reported this matter to the Blessed One.
“Monks, a bhikkhunī must not dwell in the forest.”
"If she should stay [there], there is an offense of wrong-doing.
Now at that time, a certain lay follower had given a storeroom to the community of nuns.
They reported this matter to the Blessed One.
“I allow, monks, a loft,” [the Blessed One said].
The loft was not sufficient.
They reported this matter to the Blessed One.
“I allow you, monks, a dwelling place.
The dwelling places were not sufficient.
They reported this matter to the Blessed One.
“Monks, I allow new construction work.
Yet the new construction work was not being carried out.
They reported this matter to the Blessed One.
“I allow you, monks, to make [a dwelling] even for an individual.
Now at that time, a certain woman who was pregnant had gone forth among the bhikkhunīs.
Once she had gone forth, her pregnancy came to term.
Then it occurred to that bhikkhunī:
“How now should I proceed regarding this child?
They reported this matter to the Blessed One.
“I allow you, monks, to support [the child] until that boy reaches the age of discretion.
Then it occurred to that bhikkhunī:
“I am not permitted to live alone, and another bhikkhunī is not permitted to live with a young boy. How, then, should I proceed?”
They reported this matter to the Blessed One.
“Monks, I allow you, having appointed one nun, to give her as a companion to that [other] nun.
And thus, monks, should she be appointed:”
First, a bhikkhunī should be requested; having requested her, a competent and capable bhikkhunī should inform the Saṅgha:
“Let the noble Saṅgha listen to me.
If it seems appropriate to the Saṅgha, let the Saṅgha appoint the bhikkhunī named so-and-so as the companion for the bhikkhunī named so-and-so.”
This is the motion.
Let the noble Saṅgha hear me:
the Saṅgha appoints the bhikkhunī named so-and-so as the companion for the bhikkhunī named so-and-so.
Whichever noble lady approves of the appointment of the nun named so-and-so as the companion of the nun named so-and-so, let her be silent;
whichever does not approve, let her speak.
The nun named so-and-so has been appointed by the Saṅgha as the companion of the nun named so-and-so.
“The Saṅgha consents; therefore it is silent. Thus do I understand this.
Then it occurred to that second nun:
“How now should I proceed regarding this child?”
They reported this matter to the Blessed One.
“Monks, I allow you to deal with that child in the same way as you would deal with any other man, except for the case of one who has a wife.
Now at that time, a certain bhikkhunī had committed a grave offense (garudhamma) and was undergoing the period of penance (mānatta).
Then it occurred to that bhikkhunī:
"I cannot dwell alone, and no other bhikkhunī can dwell with me; how, then, should I proceed?
They reported this matter to the Blessed One.
“Monks, I allow you to appoint one nun and give her as a companion to that nun.
And thus, monks, she should be appointed.
First, a nun should be requested; having requested her, the Saṅgha should be informed by a competent and capable nun:”
‘Let the Saṅgha, noble ladies, hear me.
If it seems appropriate to the Saṅgha, the Saṅgha should appoint the bhikkhunī named so-and-so as the companion of the bhikkhunī named so-and-so.
This is the motion.
"Let the noble Saṅgha hear me.
The Saṅgha appoints the bhikkhunī named so-and-so as the companion of the bhikkhunī named so-and-so.
Whichever noble lady approves of the appointment of the bhikkhunī named so-and-so as the companion of the bhikkhunī named so-and-so, let her be silent."
"Whoever does not approve, let her speak.
The nun named so-and-so is appointed by the Saṅgha as the companion of the nun named so-and-so.
It is pleasing to the Saṅgha; therefore, by silence, I hold this to be so."
Now at that time, a certain bhikkhunī, having renounced the training, left the order.
She returned again and requested full ordination from the bhikkhunīs.
They reported this matter to the Blessed One.
“Monks, there is no renouncing of the training for a bhikkhunī;
as soon as she has left the community, she is no longer a bhikkhunī.
Now at that time, a certain bhikkhunī went from her own residence to a sectarian fold.
She returned again and requested full ordination from the bhikkhunīs.
They reported this matter to the Blessed One.
"Bhikkhus, that bhikkhunī who, having been in her own residence, has gone over to another sectarian order, should not be ordained upon her return."
Now at that time, the bhikkhunīs—being scrupulous—did not consent to being greeted by men, nor to having their hair cut, nor to having their nails cut, nor to the treatment of wounds.
They reported this matter to the Blessed One.
“I allow you, bhikkhus, to consent,” he said.
Now at that time, the bhikkhunīs were sitting cross-legged, relishing the touch of their heels.
They reported this matter to the Blessed One.
"Bhikkhus, a bhikkhunī must not sit cross-legged."
“Whoever should sit [in this manner], there is an offense of wrong-doing.
Now at that time, a certain bhikkhunī was ill;
for her, it was not comfortable without sitting cross-legged.
They reported this matter to the Blessed One.
“I allow, monks, a half-pallaṅka for a bhikkhunī.
Now at that time, the bhikkhunīs were defecating in the restroom.
The group of six bhikkhunīs caused an abortion right there.
They reported this matter to the Blessed One.
"Bhikkhus, a bhikkhunī must not defecate in a latrine."
Whoever should do so, there is an offense of wrong-doing (*dukkaṭa*).
“I allow you, monks, to defecate in a place that is open below and covered above.
Now at that time, the bhikkhunīs were bathing with bath-powder.
People criticized, complained, and spread it about, saying,
“…just like householders who enjoy sensual pleasures.
